title: Wendell and the Confession
premise: When coroner Oscar Joubert is handed the diary of missing schoolteacher Ada Voss, they expect a grief-stricken record ending on the day she vanished. Instead, the entries continue for three more weeks—written in Ada's hand, describing places only she could know, and naming a witness to something terrible: the town's beloved patriarch, Wendell Marsh. As the trial of the accused drifter approaches, Oscar must find the one person everyone swears is dead, discovering that Ada faked her disappearance to survive and that half of Hollow Creek helped bury the truth. In the end, Oscar chooses truth over belonging, testifying alongside a living Ada as the town's careful silence finally collapses.
about_author: Dominic Kavanagh spent fifteen years as a rural court reporter before turning to fiction, drawing on the small silences he watched communities keep. He writes from a farmhouse in upstate New York, where he still attends local trials for pleasure.

chapters.title: The Diary That Kept Writing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A fisherman finds Ada Voss's diary in a culvert; Oscar, cataloguing it as evidence, realizes entries continue past her disappearance date. The final entry names Wendell Marsh as a witness to something unspeakable. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the moment a familiar world tilts.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Establishing Hollow Creek: Oscar's intimacy with its dead, their outsider status, and the town's warm deference to Wendell Marsh. They visit the Marsh estate under pretense of a death certificate and notice Wendell's son Daniel flinch at Ada's name. Emotional beat: unease beneath belonging.

chapters.title: Three Weeks of Ghost
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, interleaved with diary excerpts. The post-disappearance entries describe a boathouse, a blue coat, a woman humming in a diner—clues suggesting Ada lived hidden nearby. Sheriff Ruiz dismisses it as trauma fiction. Emotional beat: obsession kindling against institutional shrugging.

chapters.title: What the Drifter Said
chapters.summary: Oscar visits the accused drifter, Cole Brennan, in county jail. He claims innocence but refuses to say what he saw that night at the quarry, protecting someone. His lawyer warns Oscar off. Emotional beat: sympathy for the condemned and first hint of a conspiracy of silence.

chapters.title: The Blue Coat
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following the diary's diner clue, Oscar finds a waitress who remembers 'the sad teacher' buying coffee weeks after she vanished—and remembers who else asked about her: Daniel Marsh. Someone has been erasing traces ahead of Oscar. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing they are also hunted.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Small Town
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Ruiz confronts Oscar: drop it or lose their position; the town council quietly revokes their morgue access. Old friends go cold. Oscar's late mother's history with the Marshes surfaces—Oscar owes Wendell a debt. Emotional beat: belonging weaponized, loyalty tested.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Ledger
chapters.summary: Oscar breaks into the derelict Marsh boathouse and finds a ledger of payments—hush money signed by half the town, including Ruiz—and a woman's hairpin matching Ada's. Footsteps force them to flee unseen. Emotional beat: terror fused with vindication; no going back now.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Oscar and Ada. Ada, living under a new name two counties over, learns someone is asking questions and decides to run again—until she reads about the trial date. Oscar tracks her through a library card trail. They meet; she tells him what Wendell witnessed and why she ran. Emotional beat: two invisible people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, then Oscar's. Ada reveals the full truth: she saw Wendell kill a trespassing migrant worker years ago; the diary was insurance. Wendell, tipped off by Ruiz, sends Daniel to retrieve it—Daniel instead confesses to Oscar, breaking his father's hold. Wendell confronts them at the courthouse the night before trial. Emotional beat: confession as both ruin and release.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Trial day: Ada walks in alive, the ledger entered into evidence, Cole freed, Wendell and Ruiz indicted. The town turns its back on Oscar—but a few, like Daniel, stand beside them. Oscar buries no one this time, and finally feels they belong to themselves. Emotional beat: costly, hard-won peace.
